STEP 1 - Scene: This is a simple snack of three peeled avocado wedges on a paper plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel: It is a small white paper plate, about 20 cm in diameter (side-plate size). Area = 3.14 × 10² = 314 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: The only food is avocado slices, three wedges.

STEP 4 - Area: Each wedge covers about 7–8% of the plate, so the wedges together cover about 22%. The rest of the plate is empty, so food covers about 22% of the vessel.

STEP 5 - Volume: 22% of 314 cm² = 69 cm². The wedges are thick, about 2.5 cm on average. Gross volume = 69 × 2.5 ≈ 173 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Solid avocado wedges pack densely but have a curved profile, so I use a bulk density of 0.8. 173 ml × 0.8 ≈ 138 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Avocado has about 160 kcal per 100 g. 138 g × 1.60 ≈ 221 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Three wedges look like roughly half to two-thirds of a large avocado, which would be about 120–150 g of flesh. The estimate of 138 g and 221 kcal is plausible.
